# Size table: "Size every lesson for its lecture time" in AUTHORING.md;
# check_size.py (runs before every render) warns when a lesson is too short.
#   90 min (game-math): 5–7 ideas, 10–12 Try it, 40–50 questions, 3+ Examples,
#     2+ Watch out, Warm-up (lesson B), Game challenge ~20 min, no class activity.
#   60 min (computing-systems): 2–3 ideas, 3–5 Try it, 12–20 questions,
#     Class activity ~10 min. Warm-up, Example and Watch out are optional.
# Every "Try it": go through "Check every Try it" in AUTHORING.md before you commit.
title: "Lesson title in simple English"

week: 1
lesson: 1          # numbered across the course
draft: true
ilos: [A1]         # codes from the syllabus week; text comes from course.ilos

## Warm-up: remember lesson N

Two or three keywords from the last lesson.

Remember lesson N.

## 1. Game example

Short sentences. One idea per sentence. Start from a game the students know.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2"}
One short instruction. Each question is matched with its answer
(the student taps the answer and sees at once if it is right).

::: {.match}
First question?
:   its answer

Second question?
:   its answer
:::
:::

## 2. Picture, then the rule

![Caption in simple English.](sims/name.png){width=85%}

Explain the picture. Only then show the rule or formula.

::: {.callout-note title="Example: one short title"}
1. First step, with the numbers.
2. Second step.
3. The answer in **bold**. Check it, if you can.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Watch out!"}
One common mistake, and how to avoid it.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3"}
Question about the picture. With only 1–2 questions, add wrong answers in `extra`.

::: {.match extra="wrong answer 1|wrong answer 2"}
Question about the picture?
:   the right answer

Same rule, a little harder?
:   the right answer

The reverse question (answer → question)?
:   the right answer
:::
:::
